'''Robert Stephen White''' (December 8, 1920 – April 8, 2018) was an American physicist.

== Early life and career ==
White was born in [[Ellsworth, Kansas]], the son of Byron and Sebina White. He attended [[Southwestern College (Kansas)|Southwestern College]], earning his [[Bachelor of Arts|BA degree]] in 1942. He also attended the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], earning his [[Master of Science|MS degree]] in [[physics]] in 1943. His education was interrupted when he served as a [[Officer (armed forces)|naval officer]], and developed [[thermal diffusion]] separation for the [[Manhattan Project]] during [[World War II]]. After his discharge, he attended the [[University of California, Berkeley]], earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in 1951.<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/newspress/name/robert-white-obituary?id=9647922|title=Robert White Obituary (1920-2018)|work=[[Santa Barbara News-Press]]|date=April 29, 2018|access-date=November 3, 2026|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref><ref name="b">{{Cite web|url=https://cnas.ucr.edu/news/2018/05/17/memory-robert-stephen-white|title=In Memory of Robert Stephen White|work=[[University of California, Riverside]]|date=May 17, 2018|access-date=November 3, 2026}}</ref>

White served as a professor in the department of physics at the [[University of California, Riverside]] from 1967 to 1990. During his years as a professor, he was named a [[distinguished professor]],<ref name="b" /> and in 1969, he was named a [[Lists of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=r%20stephen%20white&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=November 3, 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
In 1942, White married Freda Marie Bridgewater in [[Beaver, Oklahoma]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressenterprise.com/obituaries/memoriam-robert-white-santa-barbara-ca/|title=Robert White|work=[[The Press-Enterprise]]|date=April 29, 2018|access-date=November 3, 2026}}</ref> Their marriage lasted until her death in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/newspress/name/freda-white-obituary?id=18738006|title=Freda White Obituary (2013)|work=[[Santa Barbara News-Press]]|date=February 20, 2013|access-date=November 3, 2026|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref>

White died at his home in [[Santa Barbara, California]] on April 8, 2018, at the age of 97.<ref name="a" />
